glance: Anthropic opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq, about 34% above its $83 IPO price, valuing it near $1.5 trillion.
The Trump-Xi-Putin summit ended with a declaration on nuclear risk and UN reform but no mention of Ukraine.
Stocks are rebounding at midday, with the Nasdaq up nearly 2% on the Anthropic debut.
Nvidia's interim CEO promised earlier raises and equity at its first all-hands since Jensen Huang's exit.
Patches are out for a serious AI-discovered NGINX flaw that exposes millions of web servers.

tech.headline: Anthropic soars in Nasdaq debut
tech.summary: Anthropic's shares opened at $111.50 when trading began at 11:48 a.m. ET, about 34% above the $83 IPO price, and quickly climbed near $115, implying a market value around $1.5 trillion. The offering, priced above its $70 to $78 range, is the largest on record, and about $3 billion came from a Japanese investor tranche. The debut is being watched as a test of investor appetite for AI after weeks of tech selling.

tech.headline: Nvidia's interim chief moves to steady staff after record quarter
tech.summary: Days after Jensen Huang's exit, interim CEO Colette Kress held Nvidia's first all-hands without him and signaled pay raises and equity grants would come earlier than planned, Wired reports. The company had just posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, more than double a year ago, and guided to about $130 billion next quarter, but shares slipped Wednesday as the board ruled out reinstating Huang and began a search for a permanent CEO.

tech.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Neon
tech.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a middle tier between its top Carbon and fast Hydrogen models, across the Gemini API, Antigravity and the Gemini app for paid users, claiming top marks on a coding-agent index at $3 per million input tokens. Google also renamed its Gemini Spark agent to Tasks and made it free in six countries, and opened Genie 4 world-generation to AI Ultra subscribers.

tech.headline: AI-discovered NGINX flaw lets attackers take over servers
tech.summary: Security firm Xint used AI models to uncover five flaws in NGINX, one of the web's most widely used server programs, including an unauthenticated remote-code-execution bug dating to 2015 that works on default settings. F5, which maintains NGINX, began issuing patches Wednesday and urged immediate updates; Wiz says it found the same flaws independently. Researchers estimate millions of exposed servers could be vulnerable.

tech.headline: Palo Alto Networks buys AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B
tech.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal worth about $4.5 billion, extending its push into AI-driven security. The company also beat first-quarter revenue estimates and raised its full-year forecast, sending shares higher after hours.

tech.headline: Microsoft puts Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot
tech.summary: At its Ignite conference, Microsoft made the core Office apps generally available directly inside Copilot, pitching the assistant as the main interface for work. It is a further step in reorganizing Microsoft 365 around AI agents rather than standalone apps.

tech.headline: White House weighs making companies disclose Chinese AI use
tech.summary: The Trump administration is considering a rule requiring US firms to disclose when they use Chinese-made AI models, while new Commerce rules tighten licensing for advanced chips headed to overseas data centers serving restricted firms. In California, Gov. Gavin Newsom proposed broad new state powers to regulate AI, stopping short of mandatory kill switches.

other.headline: Trump-Xi-Putin summit ends with a declaration that skips Ukraine
other.summary: The first three-way meeting of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders ran about 90 minutes in Shenzhen with no joint press conference. A follow-up declaration covered UN reform, energy supply, criticism of ICC overreach and a pledge that nuclear war must never be fought, but said nothing about Ukraine; Kyiv insisted no deal about it can be made without it.

other.headline: Stocks rebound as Anthropic lifts the Nasdaq
other.summary: By midday the Nasdaq was up about 1.9% and the S&P 500 about 1.1%, while the Dow edged up 0.2% after three straight losses. Tech led the rebound as Anthropic began trading.

other.headline: Jobless claims tick up; Fed hike talk lingers
other.summary: Initial unemployment claims rose by 1,000 to 203,000, slightly above forecasts but still low. With inflation running hot, futures traders are pricing quarter-point Fed rate hikes in December and January, and the 10-year Treasury yield is holding above 5%.

other.headline: Officials: recent outages were not a coordinated attack
other.summary: At a House Homeland Security hearing, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, DNI Jay Clayton and the FBI said a run of outages, including an FAA ground stop, bank and Microsoft service failures, and an NSA network outage, stemmed from separate maintenance and technical changes. The FBI said it found no sign of malicious cyber activity.

other.headline: Peltola wins Alaska Senate race; Jeffries nominated for Speaker
other.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan roughly 50% to 46%, becoming the first Indigenous woman from Alaska elected to the Senate and widening the Democratic majority. House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker in the next Congress.
